content.speaker: Knut
content.text: I stumbled across some components. Lately, it seems like everyone is looking for them in their spare time. These little things can definitely come in handy.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: The little thing was hidden just behind the base of the statue. It seemed that our resilient bear had found a new home here. The old statue had to be moved to make way for it, but its base remained. I suspected it had left some of its components behind.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: Comrade Evgeni ... he did not notice the changes in Rayashki, but change is inevitable and ongoing. He was still holding onto memories of when things were tough and rough.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: In those days, this square didn't even exist. We painstakingly dug it out with shovels and carried each stone ourselves.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: No one expected Rayashki to end up so beautiful. We were never ones for making plans or dreaming big; we simply rolled up our sleeves and got to work.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: Now, Rayashki might change once more. What will it become? Everything is changing so fast. We have a pool and a school; it all seems to have been built in the blink of an eye.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: As soon as a project is completed, the difficulties and sacrifices made along the way are quickly forgotten. The immense sense of accomplishment makes us believe that all the hard work was worth it.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: I don't want to leave. I'm afraid I'll change faster than this town did. Those who come back later feel like strangers themselves.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: It's incredible, isn't it? How things can change in what feels like an instant ...

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: Factories, ores, and Rayashki!

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: To me, Rayashki seems almost like another name for Runium. Perhaps it is because I am the one responsible for sifting the ore.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: While most people came here with grand ideals, I simply signed my name on the list without much thought. It wasn't long before I found myself stepping off the train and into this unfamiliar land. Fortunately, aside from the wild Critters roaming about and the stubborn terrain, life here has been relatively simple.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: Regardless, it's all laborious work. And I understand that even Critters have to eat and survive. I forgive them.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: But back to the here and now. The factory is finally complete, and we have surpassed our wildest expectations. These accomplishments are not gifts from some higher power, but of our own making!

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: These are true miracles, not bestowed by any divine entity but created by our own hard work and determination. Just take a look around!

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: There was a time when I felt nothing, just going through the motions of everyday life. But now I finally feel like I am making a difference. It may not be extraordinary, but it's more than most people achieve in their lives.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: Yes, I couldn't have done this alone. It's a rare opportunity to find others willing to work alongside you, swinging hammers and building something meaningful together.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: I hope to turn our experiences here into a legend, like the stories of Comrade Evgeni. With a little exaggeration, of course. Young people need these legends to inspire them.

content.speaker: Adrian
content.text: So let's raise a glass to the new factory and all that we have accomplished here together!

trails.title: A Promise
trails.description: I believe we are resilient and strong, and I have no doubt that you are too.

content.text: Vibrant Snowy Square

Take another good look at the square. It hasn't changed much—a polar bear stands in the center, outlined by a faint light, while children eagerly reach out to touch its paws. The snow dusts the bear's head, giving it a serene quality that contrasts with the lively setting. Flowers bloom amidst the white snow, covering most of the stones on the ground. The bear appears to be at peace against the mustard yellow background.

    This is an important place in Rayashki, as the town kitchen cannot accommodate such a large number of people. It is often used for public discussions and will continue to serve that purpose. Recently, it was decided to allow children to venture outside and explore the world beyond. The road leading there is bathed in sunlight, decorated with red ribbons that sway in the gentle breeze from the trees.

    People find familiar images here that evoke nostalgia and memories of past lives, yet those who come here rarely speak of their homeland. This is the true essence of Rayashki—everything they hoped to see in their homeland, but never did. It's like the distant horizon that Rusalka dreams of as she braves the icy waters, or the intricate illustrations created by traveling ley hunters, or even the homes of Foundation visitors who have long since disappeared. It's what previous generations promised the next: a glimpse of their idealized homeland.

   The more impossible an ideal seems, the stronger it becomes—unbreakable in its perceived perfection.

    Despite this, there is still so much to strive for and achieve in life.

items.text: People's Square, Rayashki
The people gather again.
This time, though, there are no more disputes, no resentment.
This is a gathering of joy.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: After thorough discussion, the people of Rayashki have made their final decision.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I stand here to declare the future direction of Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: As of today, Rayashki will be no longer affiliated with any organizations, and all factories dedicated to processing of runium ore will be shut down.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: What are we going to do for our work, then?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: I don't want to sit around at home living on benefits!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There will be many things to do, Comrade Valeriya.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: As the elites above us struggle for power, we ordinary people suffer in darkness.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But now, there will be a new source of power, one built to lift up the people not to take from them. And it will run on Rayashki coal.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We will start new factories in Rayashki and explore the possibilities of working with other coal producers nearby.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We will mine with our own hands and feed ourselves.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Maybe we can even build a dock and sell our products far away.
The people chatter excitedly.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We will raise a new banner above Rayashki, one welcoming all ordinary people ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: ... to come to a livable place with abundant power and job opportunities for their future.
Arms and smiles intermingle, then a rising wave of applause.
The wave washes over everyone, including Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What about your plan, Comrade Windsong?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I think I'm going to stay for a while.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You need to know that for now we must tighten our belts. Everyone's rations must be cut for some time until Rayashki gets back on its feet.
The researcher does not waver, not in the slightest.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: At least for now, the study of ley lines belongs here, not in the fancy halls and symposiums of human academia.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This place still holds many possible research avenues: monitoring the changes in the environment, further detailing the local ley energy map, maybe even studying the mutation of the Kikituks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I must finish them to further develop the study before it is ready for academia again.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Then it sounds like you may be with us for a long time yet, good.
They exchange smiles.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And don't forget, you are expected to cut the ribbon at the ceremony.
An enthusiastic hand reaches out to Windsong once again.
Now, the little arctic town is covered in a strange mix of black coal soot and bright yellow flowers, a warm wind blowing over every inch of soil and each wall, old and new.
It flows like blood through snow-white skin and fluffy pores. A scene like a hand-drawn picture.
Windsong walks alone through the town, feeling the energy of the earth beneath her.
Townsfolk pass her.
They nod and greet her with hopeful smiles.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Windsong, I want to apologize for being rude to you during class.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: I'll bring you some Friendship cheese next time, to apologize. I promise!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: You will always be our comrade.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Hats off to you!
In the distance, children cluster around a vibrant field of sunflowers.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ms. Windsong!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I think we performed very well at the ceremony!
The boy, bright as any other sunflower, waves to her as he hops joyfully in the snow.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Will you come teach us again?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: We want to learn more, too!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Same here!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ms. Windsong, the sunflowers we planted are blooming!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: We protected the town!
Windsong wants to say something, but a sudden creaking draws up her attention.
She looks up to see a construction crane looming over the town.
The new coal refinery, a school, a hockey field, the dormitories ...
In the boundless future ahead for Rayashki, these buildings will be like speckled grains of sand cast over the tundra.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We begin the next chapter of Rayashki today.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm so glad we will build it together.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hello, Rayashki.
